'''J. Michael Scott''' (born September 21, 1941) is an American scientist, professor, [[environmentalist]] and [[author]].

== Early life and education ==
Scott is the eldest son of [[Eileen Rose Busby]],<ref>[http://www.signonsandiego.com/uniontrib/20050409/news_1m9busby.html Eileen Rose Busby; writer, world traveler and antiques expert | ''The San Diego Union-Tribune''<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071021134812/http://www.signonsandiego.com/uniontrib/20050409/news_1m9busby.html |date=2007-10-21 }}</ref> an author and [[antiques]] expert, and [[James (Jim) Scott|Jim Scott]], a [[Senior Olympics]] winner who helped pioneer and develop the game of [[racquetball]]. He is the grandson of California [[artist]] [[Esther Rose (painter)|Esther Rose]], the nephew of the late Russian Orthodox Hieromonk [[Seraphim Rose]], brother of true crime author [[Cathy Scott]] and volunteer [[Cordelia Mendoza]].

A graduate of [[San Diego County]]'s [[Helix High School]], Scott attended the [[University of Redlands]] for one year before earning his [[Bachelor's Degree|bachelor's]] and [[master's degree]]s in [[marine biology]] from [[San Diego State University]] and a [[doctorate]] in [[ornithology]] from [[Oregon State University]].

== Career ==
He is a senior scientist with the [[U.S. Geological Survey]], a leader with the Idaho Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research and a professor of Fish and Wildlife Resources at the [[University of Idaho]].<ref>[http://www.cnrhome.uidaho.edu/default.aspx?pid=72860 Dr. Scott – Department of Fish & Wildlife Resources<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100605030919/http://www.cnrhome.uidaho.edu/default.aspx?pid=72860 |date=2010-06-05 }}</ref>

In 1963, Scott joined the [[Peace Corps]] and served a two-year stint in [[Cartago, Valle del Cauca|Cartago]], [[Colombia]], where he founded a natural history museum, started a [[Red Cross]] swimming program, and coached a number of sports.

From 1974 to 1984, Scott served as a research [[biologist]] for the [[U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service]] at [[Mauna Loa]] Field Station in [[Hawaii Volcanoes National Park]]. It was his first assignment with the [[U.S. Department of Interior]]. From 1984 to 1986, he served as project leader of the [[California Condor]] Research Center in Ventura. In 1986 he was appointed to his current position as leader of the Idaho Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit in Moscow, Idaho. In addition, he is a professor in the Department of Fish and Wildlife Resources at the [[University of Idaho]], where he pioneered the [[Gap Analysis Program]] and served as program leader from 1989 to 1997.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cnrhome.uidaho.edu/fishwild/Scott |title=Dr. Scott – Department of Fish & Wildlife Resources |access-date=2007-03-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070407085706/http://www.cnrhome.uidaho.edu/fishwild/Scott |archive-date=2007-04-07 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Scott is an elected fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and the [[American Ornithologists' Union]]. Also, he is a past president of both The Cooper Ornithological Society<ref>[http://www.cooper.org/ Home page, The Cooper Ornithological Society<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> and the Pacific Seabird Group,<ref name="PacificSeabird">[http://www.pacificseabirdgroup.org/ Pacific Seabird Group (PSG) Website:<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> and has served on the boards of a number of professional societies and the science advisory boards of several non-profit conservation organizations.<ref name="AouConservation">{{Cite web |url=http://www.redorbit.com/news/science/848814/aou_conservation_award_2006_j_michael_scott/index.html?source=r_science |title=Aou Conservation Award, 2006: J. Michael Scott – Science – redOrbit<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2007-03-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930030913/http://www.redorbit.com/news/science/848814/aou_conservation_award_2006_j_michael_scott/index.html?source=r_science |archive-date=2007-09-30 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Scott">{{cite journal|last=Scott|first=J. === Awards ===

In April 2011, Scott was awarded the rank of [[Distinguished Professor|Distinguished Emeritus Professor]] from the University of Idaho. The distinguished professor rank, which was given to two other professors in addition to Scott, was done to recognize "sustained excellence, as judged by peers, in scholarly, creative, and artistic achievement; breadth and depth of teaching in their discipline; and university service as well as service involving the application of scholarship, creative, or artistic activities that address the needs of one or more external publics," according to a news release.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.uidaho.edu/sci/newsevents/viewpost?name=honoring-excellence-university-of-idaho-honors-faculty-establishes-university-distinguished-professor-rank |title=Honoring Excellence: University of Idaho Honors Faculty |access-date=2011-10-20 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120805223324/http://www.uidaho.edu/sci/newsevents/viewpost?name=honoring-excellence-university-of-idaho-honors-faculty-establishes-university-distinguished-professor-rank |archive-date=2012-08-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
He received the American Ornithologist's Union 2006 Conservation Award,<ref>[http://www.aou.org/awards/awardees.php3 AOU | Awards | Recipients<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> an International award presented for extraordinary scientific contributions by an individual to the conservation, restoration, or preservation of birds and their habitats. Scott is a past president of both [[The Cooper Ornithological Society]]<ref>[http://www.cooper.org/ Home<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> and the [[Pacific Seabird Group]],<ref name="PacificSeabird" /> and has served on the boards of a number of professional societies and the science advisory boards of several non-profit conservation organizations.<ref name="AouConservation" /><ref name="Scott" />

In 2010, he was honored by the nonprofit [[Defenders of Wildlife]] with its Spirit of Defenders Award for Public Service.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.defenders.org/about_us/awards_dinner.php |title=Given Spirit of Defenders Award for Public Service, Sept. 22, 2010 |access-date=2010-09-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101010131349/http://www.defenders.org/about_us/awards_dinner.php |archive-date=2010-10-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2006, Scott received the U.S. Department of Interior's Distinguished Service Award,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.spokesmanreview.com/tools/story_pf.asp?ID=133599 |title=SR.com: UI wildlife professor cited for distinguished service<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2007-03-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070926214727/http://www.spokesmanreview.com/tools/story_pf.asp?ID=133599 |archive-date=2007-09-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.today.uidaho.edu/details.aspx?id=3522 |title=Today@Idaho – News Article<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2008-05-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081216042652/http://www.today.uidaho.edu/details.aspx?id=3522 |archive-date=2008-12-16 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the highest award given to a career employee for a lifetime of service. Also, his professional accomplishments have been recognized by the [[Society for Conservation Biology]] with both the Distinguished Achievement Award and the Edward T. La Roe III Memorial Award. He received a Twentieth Century Environmental Achiever Award at the Ninth Lukac's Symposium.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.climatescience.gov/Library/sap/sap4-4/sap4-4prospectus-final.htm |title=Final Prospectus for: Preliminary review of adaptation options for climate-sensitive ecosystems and resources<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=2007-03-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070701104040/http://www.climatescience.gov/Library/sap/sap4-4/sap4-4prospectus-final.htm |archive-date=2007-07-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
